title: Ayr truck route study and transit software
subtitle: MobilityPLUS scheduling software, Oxford Road 5 transfer from Wilmot, and tracking list updates on safety zones and an Elmira bypass.
overview: The committee recommended that the Region study truck traffic in downtown Ayr and look at interim measures such as warning signage, lower speeds in busy pedestrian areas and outreach to the trucking industry {{vote:m2}}. Staff said they would explore interim steps promptly and consider capital measures for the 2025 capital plan, with a report back in the August cycle. This matters to Ayr residents and businesses because of reported safety problems and damage to infrastructure.

The committee also recommended assigning a new project manager to speed up updates to the MobilityPLUS scheduling software used by Grand River Transit {{vote:m1}}. Staff said the project manager comes from existing Information Technology Services staff, not a new hire. The software is meant to make better use of existing vehicles and operators.

The committee received an update on transferring Oxford Road 5 from Wilmot Township to the Region. Staff expect to bring a recommendation to Council by fall 2024, once a safety project at Punkeydoodle's Corners is finished. The tracking list will show the Community Safety Zone update for August 2024. Staff also agreed to add Oxford Road 5 and the Elmira bypass study to it.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region study options for truck traffic on Northumberland St. in downtown Ayr, including a possible truck ban, and explore interim measures such as signage, speed reductions and industry communication.
The committee recommended assigning a new project manager to speed up updates to the MobilityPLUS scheduling software, as outlined in report TSD-TRS-24-006.

debate: On Ayr, the sponsoring councillor said delegates raised safety concerns about narrow downtown streets, damage to infrastructure and to trucks, and reduced foot traffic. The aim was a solution workable for both businesses and residents.

One councillor questioned why enforcement was not focused on a nearby road built for trucks and upgraded by the Region. That councillor suggested signage directing drivers to it, while also supporting work with staff.
Councillors asked for a timeline on the Ayr interim measures. Staff said some study is needed first, so June was not realistic, and the August cycle was agreed.
On MobilityPLUS, a councillor asked whether this meant a new employee. Staff said it would put the project at the top of the list for an existing IT project manager.

On Oxford Road 5, councillors asked about delays and road condition. Staff said delays were partly procedural and partly due to a policy review. Two of three key costs were known, and the cost of any improvements to bring the road up to standard was not yet known.
